annotation.authors_or_issuer: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (with federal, provincial and territorial privacy authorities)
key_provisions_or_claims: Generative AI is subject to existing Canadian privacy laws; organizations must have legal authority and valid, meaningful consent for personal information used.
Developers and users should conduct Privacy Impact Assessments and Algorithmic Impact Assessments.
Organizations must tell affected people when generative AI is used in decisions, and give recourse.
Special attention to children and groups historically facing discrimination; test training data for bias.
Establish accountability structures, traceable outputs, and safeguards against misuse and security risks.
annotation.summary_en: Joint guidance from Canada's federal, provincial and territorial privacy authorities applying key privacy principles to generative AI. It says generative AI is covered by existing privacy law and sets expectations for developers, providers and users on legal authority and consent, necessity, openness, accountability, safety and protection of vulnerable groups.
annotation.title_clean: Principles for responsible, trustworthy and privacy-protective generative AI technologies
annotation.title_en: Principles for responsible, trustworthy and privacy-protective generative AI technologies
